Flavio Bolsonaro claims he is Brazil’s true leader after fleeing to U.S.
 “I am the elected president, and the criminals who stole Brazil’s election are part of a criminal organization that has established a tyranny,” Flavio Bolsonaro said; U.S. President Donald Trump said he “won’t get involved” in Mr. Bolsonaro’s claim
 Updated - October 29, 2026 12:00 pm IST - MIAMI 
 AFP READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro arrives at Miami Opa-Locka Executive Airport on October 28, 2026, in Opa-locka, Florida.
 | Photo Credit: AP
 Brazil's defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro insisted on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) he is his country's rightful leader, after fleeing to the United States to start a self-imposed exile.
 Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro's defiance on arrival in Florida signalled continued upheaval for Brazil, where leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won a dramatic runoff election on Sunday (October 25, 2026).
 "I am the elected president, and the criminals who stole Brazil's election are part of a criminal organization that has established a tyranny," Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro said in the statement published on his X account, slamming "electoral fraud."
 Brazil’s Flavio Bolsonaro lands in Florida after election defeat "I will lead the opposition from here," he said. In a subsequent statement, he revised his claim, saying he is the "leader," rather than "president."
 Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro, 45, touched down earlier on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) in a private jet at Opa-Locka Executive Airport near Miami.
 Rogerio Marinho, the leader of Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro's Liberal Party in the Senate, told reporters in Brasilia that he was in "solidarity" with the former candidate, describing him as a "political exile."
 However, he distanced himself from Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro's statement, and refused to back up claims of electoral fraud.
 "The Liberal Party cannot make that claim," he said. "There is no evidence of that."
 Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro "is an expression of the right in Brazil today...he calls himself a leader and it's true: he's a leader," Mr. Marinho told reporters.
 U.S. President Donald Trump's hard-right administration has strong links to Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro and his father Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest in Brazil after attempting to overturn his own electoral loss to Lula in 2022.
 Mr. Trump reiterated his stand that Brazil's election was "very strange" but told reporters he "won't get involved" in Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro's claim to the presidency.
 Details of how Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro, accompanied by his wife and daughters, made it to U.S. soil are still emerging.
 He is under investigation in his home country over alleged corruption and money laundering. With his current parliamentary immunity about to expire, he was ordered to surrender his passports but left anyway, reaching the United States via Argentina and Ecuador.
 A police source told AFP that Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro's Brazilian and diplomatic passports had been canceled, but the senator has also held Italian nationality since 2023, according to Italian documents seen by AFP .
 The U.S. Department of Homeland Security said in a statement that the Bolsonaro family members were inspected and cleared "with applicable immigration laws and procedures."
 The travel ban was issued by powerful Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, who led the case against Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro's father and is a controversial figure hated by the Brazilian right.
 Trump would approve Flavio Bolsonaro coming to U.S.; says Brazil election was ‘very strange’ 'Shameful' act
 Mr. Lula, who won the election with 51.8% of the vote, called Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro's departure a "shameful" act.
 "A person who sneaks out of their country must have something to hide," he said in Brasilia during his 81st birthday celebration on Tuesday (October 27, 2026).
 But Brazil police issued a statement on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) saying that he was not considered a fugitive.
 There was controversy in neighboring Argentina, where opposition lawmakers demanded to know how Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro had managed to transit through the country.
 While Argentinian authorities said he was carrying valid travel documents, officials have requested chief of cabinet Diego Santilli to provide details to parliament, according to opposition lawmaker Agustin Rossi.
 Bolsonaro’s party says it recognises Lula’s election win in Brazil Fraud cases
 The most high-profile fraud case against Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro in Brazil centres on the unreleased biopic "Dark Horse" starring U.S. actor Jim Caviezel as Mr. Flavio's father Jair.
 In May, the outlet Intercept Brasil revealed audio recordings in which Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro negotiated approximately $24 million to finance the film with banker Daniel Vorcaro, who is jailed over one of Brazil's biggest-ever fraud cases.
 Brazil election ‘rigged’, says Trump without citing evidence Before the leak, Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro had denied knowing Mr. Vorcaro, or that he had financed the movie.
 In July, the Supreme Court ordered a probe into the film's financing, and whether it involved corruption, money laundering or the illegal movement of currency.
 Mr. Flavio Bolsonaro acknowledged Mr. Vorcaro had funded the film, but insisted it was a private business deal that was "completely legal."
